Interview Experience 
Mahi S. Palimkar - TY BTech CE, 231071036 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
Introduction 
Hello, I am Mahi Palimkar, currently a pre-final year student pursuing Computer 
Engineering at VJTI.  
 
This is a report which will serve as a record for my interview experience with HTSI 
for Summer Internship. 
 
 
  
Pre-Placement talk (PPT) 
The PPT for HTSI was held on 24rd of july 2025. It was the 4th company visiting 
campus after JP Morgan, DE Shaw, Goldman Sachs. 
 
So HILTI is one of those companies that tries to wrap up everything-ppt, oa, 
interviews, in a span of just 2 days.

PPT was held on the morning of 24rd July in our auditorium. There were 3 panelists 
who were present to give the ppt, Mr. Amit Samtani, Mr Tobias and Ms. Likhita who 
was the HR. 
 
The PPT was actually pretty interesting. We came to know about how HILTI is one of 
the most sought after companies in the construction sector. It is one of the very few 
companies that makes extremely high quality power tools, software, and services for 
the global construction industry. 
 
The PPT ended around 11 am. The OA was scheduled somewhere in the evening 
around 4 pm. 
 
It is important to pay attention to whatever is being said in the PPT.  Note it down, 
preferably. The various application softwares that HILTI is working on, and were 
elucidated in the PPT, came up somewhere during my interview and it was a win-win 
because I remembered that. 
 
 
 
Online Assessment 
I do not remember exactly as I am writing this a long time after the selection 
happened, but there were two dsa questions which were not too difficult, and later on 
MCQs spanning over OOPS (imp for hilti), DBMS and CN. 
 
 
Interview 
 
Technical Round 
We reported at the TPO at 8.30 a.m. in the morning. My turn came pretty late, after 
lunch actually, somewhere around 2 p.m. . I know waiting can be very anxious and 
frustrating, but there is also a silver lining to it that you come to know what questions 
people are being asked, so you are a little better prepared. 
 
There were two rounds- one technical, second HR. My technical round interviewer 
was a very senior employee in HILTI. The interview started with him skimming 
through my resume. He asked me to introduce myself. Keep an apt introduction ready. 
He was impressed by my introduction. He noticed my cgpa on the resume, which is 
good. He asked me how my OA went. These people had our oa answers and scores on 
their laptops in front of them. Be thorough with your oa solutions, there are chances 
they ask you to explain that to them. I told him it went well.

Next he asked me to explain one of my projects. He did some cross questioning on 
that, and then moved to CS fundamentals. 
HILTI gives more weightage to OOPS and DBMS. He started with OOPS. 
He asked me to explain polymorphism, its types, typically everything I knew about it. 
He asked me to write pseudo code showing both types of polymorphism. I don't 
remember exactly, but he went into great depth regarding this- everything from 
vpointers to vtables. Make sure you know all this in depth. 
He then asked me questions on the rest of the 3 pillars, but not in great depth. 
Then he moved onto DBMS, asked me to write 2 queries in SQL. They were easy. 
 
Then he moved to DSA. I was only asked one question- Stock Buy and Sell (I). 
He asked me to write proper c++ code for it and also do a dry run with an example he 
gave me. 
 
I think this was all he asked me. He told me he was done from his side, and asked me  
if I had any questions. I asked him what his position was in HILTI, what he was 
currently working on. He started explaining it to me in great detail- about how he 
was currently leading a team for a certain product. I was listening intently, and asked 
him questions about the product. He explained to me in depth about it. I asked him 
how he ended up in HILTI, again to which he had a very descriptive reply. 
So my point here basically is, try to strike up interesting conversations with the 
interviewer; it works wonders. In my interview, towards the end, it literally felt like it 
wasn't an interview and we were chatting. That put me at ease. 
 
HR Round 
After sometime, the students shortlisted for the HR round were called. There were 10 
to 11 students if I remember correctly. My turn came about third to last. The HR was 
the same lady who had come to deliver the PPT the day before. She asked me to sit 
down. I was expecting she would start with some specific questions, but she started 
with a rather open ended one; actually, not a question at all. She just simply asked me 
what I wanted to talk about. I got a little anxious because I couldn't think of anything 
to talk about.  I don't remember what I said but the conversation shifted to who 
inspires me most in life, why so, what i am doing to become a little more like them 
everyday. I happened to mention that I value good speaking skills; she started 
digging into this, asking me why do you think so, who do you look up to as a good 
speaker etc etc. Sometimes they ask you tricky questions but you must recognize 
them and try to answer correctly or diplomatically. 
 
 
After everybody's HR rounds were finished, in about 15 minutes they announced the 
results. 4 girls and 1 boy were selected, and I feel privileged to be one of them!
